phase_options_status: Unapproved alternatives; no phase or anchor is chosen here.

phase_options.name: Initial strategy versus final outcomes
phase_options.assignment: All sampled early documents: proposal_early_stage; all late documents: end_project.
phase_options.advantage: Uses the publication combined proposal/early category for initial strategies and its end category for documented outcomes. Post-award status does not itself exclude the combined early category.
phase_options.tradeoff: The <=50% bin can contain established implementation; early anchors may under-demand evidence. Different early/end requirements prevent a common-scale improvement interpretation.
phase_options.decision_needed: Justify a common initial-strategy interpretation from externally documented version purpose, then calibrate anchors separately for the two phases.

phase_options.name: Implementation checkpoint versus final outcomes
phase_options.assignment: All sampled early documents: mid_project; all late documents: end_project.
phase_options.advantage: Makes implementation/progress central for post-award DMPs and avoids treating every early sample as a proposal.
phase_options.tradeoff: An initial deliverable may legitimately contain plans before substantial data production; mid requirements can over-demand evidence. Also changes expectations across versions.
phase_options.decision_needed: State why all early issue dates/version purposes warrant implementation checks; retain missing implementation separately from inaccessible evidence.

phase_options.name: Common end-state readiness lens
phase_options.assignment: Both versions: end_project, explicitly labelled readiness against end-state expectations.
phase_options.advantage: Holds criterion wording constant for a descriptive within-pair change in documented readiness.
phase_options.tradeoff: Early plans are intentionally assessed before outcomes are due; this changes the construct from stage-appropriate sufficiency to end-state readiness. It cannot be described as the framework stage-sensitive evaluation.
phase_options.decision_needed: Approve that different estimand and calibrate what counts as evidence under the same end-state lens; do not quietly merge with phase-appropriate scores.

phase_options.name: Declared phase sensitivity analysis
phase_options.assignment: For each early document retain separate proposal_early_stage and mid_project conditions; all late documents use end_project.
phase_options.advantage: Shows whether the conclusion depends on early-phase interpretation without pretending <=50% resolves it.
phase_options.tradeoff: More human/model assessments, correlated repeat exposure and multiplicity; the primary interpretation still must be chosen before results. Mid-project 5d is instrument undefined in this condition.
phase_options.decision_needed: Freeze primary versus sensitivity condition, review exposure/order and separate records/denominators; do not choose the favorable phase after scores.

late_evidence_boundary: Issue date >100% supports a post-project sampling bin and the end concept, but does not show that completed actions are documented in the DMP. Repositories, metadata files, ELN snapshots, compliance records and final spending may be external. A DMP-only packet can establish reporting, not actual practice; inaccessible external evidence is not absence or a negative legal finding.
before_numeric_comparison: Freeze criterion/phase and packet boundary; preserve changed acceptance routes instead of assuming ID identity.
Calibrate phase-specific ordinal anchors outside the final cohort.
A distinct native human-instrument condition, if adopted, needs separate records and cannot replace framework reference judgments.
Develop and independently justify any native 0-100 versus human ordinal mapping on outside-cohort material; none is supplied or approved here.
Keep missing native criteria, instrument-undefined cells, NA, inaccessible evidence, and missing model output separate.
